verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission officially launched on Wednesday, April 1, 2026
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis 2 launched on 1 April 2026 at 6.35pm Eastern Time" (R3); "NASA’s Artemis II mission has officially lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT" (R4); "The full Moon rises behind NASA’s Artemis II... Sunday, Feb. 1, 2026... updated on... April 1, 2026" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm the launch date as April 1, 2026, described as Wednesday in context (e.g., R4, R6).

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis 2 launched on 1 April 2026 at 6.35pm Eastern Time" (R3); "NASA’s Artemis II mission has officially lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT" (R4); "lift off from launch pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center... at 6:35 p.m. ET" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone match across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "at the Kennedy Space Center" (R1); "at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R2); "from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida" (cited snippet); "from Kennedy Space Center" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly state Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA's Artemis 2 mission is a historic test flight to send astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon" (R1); "10-day mission" (R3, R4); "a 10-day journey" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as 10-day mission in nearly all sources.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission carries four astronauts around the moon
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "launching four astronauts on NASA's Artemis 2 mission around the moon" (R1); "Artemis II will carry four astronauts" (R2); "four astronauts on a 10-day moon mission" (cited snippet)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on lunar flyby trajectory.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission marks the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft... in more than 50 years" (R1); "first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972" (R3); "first time in more than 50 years" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as first beyond LEO since 1972 (Apollo 17) across sources.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission followed a postponement from early 2026
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "delayed until April 2026 at the earliest... from March 2026" (R2); "delays... originally targeted launch in November 2024... delayed until September 2025... reforecast for early 2026, but launches were called off in both February and March 2026" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail postponements from Feb/March 2026 to April.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goal is a 10-day crewed test flight around the moon
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day crewed test flight around the moon" (matches exactly in cited snippet); "historic test flight to send astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon" (R1); "pioneering crewed spaceflight... 10-day mission" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches mission description as 10-day crewed test around moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch was successful
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "successful launch of Artemis II" (R4); "NASA launches first crewed moon mission" (cited snippet); "Artemis 2 splashdown success" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All post-launch sources confirm successful liftoff and mission progress.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew reported minor technical issues with the toilet system
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "There was a little potty problem... glitch in... space toilet... minor technical issues" (R1); "problem with the toilet on Orion" (R3); "toilet system controller issue" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: R1 details minor toilet fan/controller issue reported by crew.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew continued with the mission
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "successful repair of the toilet... mission proceeding as planned" (R1); "Any issues... quickly resolved... crew in Orion orbited Earth" (R3); "mission is proceeding as planned after launch" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm issues resolved and mission continued without interruption.

verifications.claim: Backup opportunities for the Artemis II launch were scheduled for April 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and April 30, 2026 if a launch had not occurred on April 1
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If the mission cannot launch on April 1, the next available launch window dates and times are: April 2: 6:22 pm CDT April 3: 7:00 pm CDT April 4: 7:53 pm CDT April 5: 8:40 pm CDT April 6: 9:36 pm CDT April 30: 5:06 pm CDT" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: R2 lists exact backup dates matching the claim.
